{"content":"Below is a concise guide on how to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance equipped with an **NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU** running **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> **Note:** Google Cloud does not use the term *EC2* – that is AWS terminology. In GCP the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Item | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Project ID | Your GCP project identifier. |
| Zone | The zone where you want to launch the instance (e.g., `us-central1-a`). |
| Service Account | An account with the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role. |
| Billing | Ensure billing is enabled for your project. |
| Compute Engine API | Enabled in the Cloud Console. |

## 2. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# Set your project and zone
export PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
export ZONE="us-central1-a"

# Create the instance
# - Machine type: n1-standard-8 (8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM)
# - GPU: NVIDIA RTX A6000 (1 GPU)
# - Boot disk: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
# - Install GPU drivers automatically via metadata

gcloud compute instances create "rtx-a6000-ubuntu" \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true \
  --service-account=your-service-account@${PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### Explanation of Key Flags
| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | Defines CPU and memory resources. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Specifies the OS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | Sets the size and type of the boot disk. |
| `--metadata=install-nvidia-driver=true` | Automatically installs the NVIDIA driver after boot. |
| `--service-account` | Grants the instance permissions. |
| `--scopes` | Provides the necessary OAuth scopes. |
| `--tags` | Enables HTTP/HTTPS traffic if needed. |

## 3. Using the REST API

If you prefer to use the REST API directly, you can send a POST request to the following endpoint:

```
POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/instances
```

Replace `{PROJECT_ID}` and `{ZONE}` with your actual values.

### Request Body (JSON)

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        {"type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT"}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "your-service-account@{PROJECT_ID}.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {"key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true"}
    ]
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/{PROJECT_ID}/zones/{ZONE}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### Authentication

Use OAuth 2.0 with a bearer token that has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` scope. You can obtain a token via the `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token` command.

### Example cURL Request

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/${PROJECT_ID}/zones/${ZONE}/instances"
```

Replace `@instance.json` with the path to the JSON file containing the request body.

---

## 4. Post‑Creation Steps

1. **Verify GPU Availability**: SSH into the instance and run `nvidia-smi` to confirm the GPU is detected.
2. **Install CUDA Toolkit** (if required): Follow NVIDIA's official instructions for installing CUDA on Ubuntu 20.04.
3. **Configure Firewall Rules**: If you need external access, ensure the appropriate firewall rules are in place.

---

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Issue | Possible Cause | Fix |
|-------|----------------|-----|
| GPU not detected | Driver not installed | Ensure `install-nvidia-driver=true` metadata is set. |
| Instance fails to start | Insufficient quota | Request a GPU quota increase in the Cloud Console. |
| Network connectivity issues | Firewall rules | Add `allow-ssh`, `allow-http`, `allow-https` rules. |

---

**Happy Cloud Computing!**

"},"filename":"create_gcp_instance_with_rtx_a6000.md"}
